extraction.title: OAuth credential sync and app integration enhancements
extraction.head: oauth-security-enhanced

greptile.text: Paraphrase: The bot summarizes the PR as adding OAuth utility reorganization into _utils/oauth and a centralized refreshOAuthTokens flow, gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, routing token refresh through a credential sync endpoint, with a webhook at /api/webhook/app-credential and AES256 encryption. Confidence score of 2/5, citing auth-breaking logic errors, a missing prisma import in the Salesforce CalendarService, invalid Zod syntax in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, and security issues in the webhook and googlecalendar callback.
Paraphrase: Style note suggesting an explicit boolean conversion (!!) for APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, since it currently relies on truthy string evaluation.

Paraphrase: Logic concern that refreshOAuthTokens may return a raw fetch Response when using the sync endpoint, so the return type may not match HubspotToken and property access later in the function would break.
Paraphrase: Syntax issue that prisma is used in the credential update without being imported. Suggests adding a prisma import from @calcom/prisma to the imports section.
Paraphrase: Logic issue that refreshOAuthTokens is passed credentialId where it expects userId. Notes Google Calendar passes credential.userId and suggests checking other integrations.
Paraphrase: Syntax issue that computed property keys using z.string().toString() are not valid Zod schema syntax and will cause runtime errors. Suggests a corrected schema.
Paraphrase: Logic issue that the key generation command (openssl rand -base64 24) yields 24 bytes, but AES256 needs 32 bytes. Suggests using -base64 32 or clarifying the requirement.
Paraphrase: Logic issue that the handler accepts any HTTP method, so it should reject non-POST requests (e.g., return 405). Suggests adding a method check.
Paraphrase: Logic issue that comparing the webhook secret with direct string equality is vulnerable to timing attacks. Suggests crypto.timingSafeEqual().
Paraphrase: Logic issue that JSON.parse and symmetricDecrypt have no error handling, so malformed data would cause runtime errors.
Paraphrase: Logic issue that falling back to an empty string for the encryption key defeats the earlier security check. Suggests throwing an error if the key is missing.
